title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were not designed to handle the specific conditions they encountered: prolonged gridlock with heavy traffic volume, unplanned road closures, and the duration of immobility required to drain their batteries. The system operated within San Francisco, a city where it had been deployed, but during a major holiday event that created traffic patterns and demands outside its normal operating envelope. Battery management under extended stationary conditions in traffic, not active driving, caused the failure.

The deployment lacked a safeguard for this scenario: either the ability to predict and avoid such congestion before batteries depleted, or a constraint that prevented operation when forecasted conditions matched those that would strand vehicles. One vehicle also caught fire after running over fireworks on a street, showing the system's inability to detect and avoid hazards created by the surrounding event environment. It is not established whether Waymo had modeled this type of holiday-driven disruption or considered it an acceptable risk of urban operation.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when heavy traffic drained their batteries. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up after a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had ignited on the street, though no injuries were reported.

The gridlock frustrated residents, with one driver reporting spending nearly two hours stuck in traffic while people yelled at the driverless cars. Waymo stated that its roadside assistance team cleared the vehicles and that the company is evaluating ways to improve performance during major traffic events. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated plans to discuss the incident with stakeholders to ensure a smoother experience at future events. This marks the second major disruption for Waymo in San Francisco, following a December power outage that affected service.
